title: Secure and Private Federated Learning: Achieving Adversarial Resilience through Robust Aggregation

C-a.quote: This median approach is applied before the SSE-based segmentation method in our rKrum algorithm (prior work).
C-a.locator: Sec. 3; the median filter is INTERNAL MACHINERY OF ONE MECHANISM rather than a second mechanism composed with it. Its stated job is to repair an estimate the Krum-derived rule needs -- "To mitigate the impact of the extreme updates on our SSE-based estimation method, we introduce a median-based filtering method that effectively removes extreme values before the estimation" (Sec. 1) and "We implement a median-based filtering algorithm to remove extreme model updates to mitigate the underestimation of f" (Sec. 3) -- and it operates on the sorted array of pairwise distances inside that estimation, "given a sorted array of distances Di′ , we fir[st]" (Sec. 3), not on the client updates that are later aggregated. AMENDMENT 3 EXCLUDES THE SECOND INNOVATION INDEPENDENTLY: the multi-update averaging's stated purpose is stability, not resisting poisoned updates -- "Stability Enhancement via Multi-Aggregation: To further improve the stability of our rKrum algorithm, we adopt a strategy inspired by multi-Krum (mKrum)" (Sec. 1). Both routes to the count therefore fail, and they fail for different reasons

C-b.quote: By combining these two enhancements, we develop an improved version of rKrum, which we call Av[erage-rKrum]
C-b.locator: Sec. 3; the composition is reported as a fact about how the algorithm was built, and each enhancement is justified against a deficiency of the AUTHORS' OWN PRIOR ALGORITHM rather than by a property that makes the two complement each other. No quotation anywhere gives a reason for pairing the median filter with the multi-update averaging; searches for complementarity, joint use and however/but adjacent to either component returned only comparisons among the five aggregators

C-c.quote: Fig. 3: Performance comparison of five aggregation algorithms on IID vs. NonIID settings under the Noise Injection attack on the MNIST dataset.
C-c.locator: Sec. 4; the assembled algorithm's own global model accuracy and round-to-round stability under attack are the evidence, reported across IID and non-IID (Dirichlet α = 0.5) settings and several attacks against Krum, mKrum, rKrum and Mean

C-d.quote: These results demonstrate the benefit of aggregating multiple client updates (as done in ArKrum and mKrum) for improving the robustness and stability of rKrum and Krum.
C-d.locator: Sec. 4; the paper's evaluation is a MENU OF ALTERNATIVE AGGREGATORS (Krum, mKrum, rKrum, ArKrum, Mean), which the rubric explicitly declines as C-a and which cannot serve as an identifying contrast either. The one comparison that looks like a within-defense arm, rKrum against ArKrum, changes BOTH innovations at once -- "By combining these two enhancements, we develop an improved version of rKrum" (Sec. 3) -- so the aggregation rule downstream is not held fixed while the upstream filter varies; it changes from single-update selection to multi-update averaging in the same step. The quotation above shows the paper itself reads that comparison off the DOWNSTREAM change, attributing the difference to multi-update averaging and never isolating the median filter. Three probes for a with/without-median arm returned one hit, the contributions list, and no arm. Rule 4 cannot rescue this: it forgives imperfection in an experiment plausibly holding a downstream mechanism fixed, and no experiment here is of that form

C-e.quote: The reason is that the injected random noise is less extreme, resulting in smaller deviations from the true model updates.
C-e.locator: Sec. 4, explaining why the Krum-family algorithms behave as they do under Noise Injection; a second, sharper mechanism attribution names the failure mode of the multi-update stage, "selecting a compromised update in the early stage of their aggregation leads to incorrect final updates, ultimately causing the mKrum and ArKrum algorithms to fail under this attack", and the C-d quotation is a third

coder_note:
C-a = NO IS THE DECIDING CODE AND IT HAS TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES, WHICH IS WHY THIS ROW IS NOT A CLOSE CALL. Route one is the structural reading: the median filter runs INSIDE the f-estimation subroutine, on the array of pairwise distances that the Krum-derived score already computes, in order to stop f from being underestimated. It never sees a client update as such and nothing is aggregated between it and the selection rule. That is one mechanism in stages, the same call made for refined-Krum (2311.15894) and for MASA's fusion step, and consistency across those three rows matters more here than any single reading. Route two is Amendment 3: the paper's OTHER innovation, multi-update averaging, is purposed for stability and non-IID performance rather than for resisting poisoned updates, so even a reader who counts the median filter as a mechanism cannot reach two without inferring a purpose the paper does not state. A5 can cite this row as the case where Amendment 3 and the structural test agree, in contrast to LASA and RKD where the amendment overturned the name-based reading.

THE TITLE IS A FALSE SIGNAL AND IT BELONGS IN A5's LIST OF THEM. The paper is titled "Secure and Private Federated Learning", but there is no privacy mechanism in it: all eleven privacy hits are either FL's baseline no-raw-data property, a promise in the abstract ("designed to enhance both the resilience and privacy guarantees of FL systems"), or descriptions of OTHER people's homomorphic-encryption work in the related section. Non-negotiable 12's purpose-quotation requirement for the privacy class therefore does not apply to this row, and the screening tags (distance-select, robust-agg) are correct where the title is not. This is a third false signal after SPFL's reputation tag and refined-Krum's secure-agg tag, and it is the first that comes from the TITLE rather than from the tagger.

WHAT WOULD HAVE MADE C-d = YES, for the counterfactual record: rKrum-with-median-filter against rKrum-without, holding the single-update selection rule fixed. The paper had every reason to run it -- the median filter is the first of its two claimed contributions -- and instead bundled it with a change to the aggregation rule, then credited the observed gain to the OTHER change. So this is not a paper that lacked the apparatus; it is a paper whose only component-level comparison confounds its two components and whose own reading of that comparison identifies neither.

SMALLEST PAPER IN THE FRAME (36374 characters) and the only one so far whose contribution is an increment on the authors' own prior algorithm. Its inclusion is correct under the frozen screen -- it proposes and evaluates a defense against Byzantine clients -- and it is a useful denominator row precisely because the DESIGN criteria fail at the first step rather than at C-b or C-d.
